notes: This is the developer SELF-TEST phase for the completed Stage A-I delivery build on feature/budgeting-app (latest commit d17ba8e at assignment time). No product code was modified in this phase, per the developer-loop skill's Test-only restriction; all writes are under developer/evidence/ plus this report.

All check-suite commands were re-run fresh from the repo root today (2026-07-31) rather than trusted from build-report.md: npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test -w server, npm run test:integration -w server, npm test -w client, npm run coverage, npm run build, npm run smoke (against a really-running server), npm run workflow:validate, and npm audit --omit dev. Results matched build-report.md's prior numbers except for format:check, which build-report.md never ran in any of its four batches.

Real-user-journey verification used two methods against a really-running server (node server/src/index.js, SERVE_CLIENT=true, ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true, NODE_ENV=development, non-production): (1) real HTTP via curl with a cookie jar for register/login/session-restore/logout, budget view, add+delete expense, plan create/edit, and insights with/without comparison; (2) a headless Playwright (chromium) session driving the actual built pages for the same journeys, confirming both the API and the rendered UI agree.

Financial reconciliation against roadmap Section 2.2 confirmed today: incomeMinor 1,250,000 / plannedMinor 1,020,000 / availableMinor 230,000 / actualMinor 842,000 (12,500 / 10,200 / 2,300 / 8,420 in display units); previousTotalMinor 918,000 (9,180); donut sharePercent [47,18,10,11,14] sums to exactly 100 via the largest-remainder rule; all values are integers throughout every API response inspected.

Playwright (chromium 130) was installed into the session scratchpad only (not the repo), after working around a local TLS-inspecting network appliance (issuer CN=Cato Networks Root CA, the corporate root already trusted by the OS/curl) that Node's bundled CA bundle does not trust by default. NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS was pointed at that same OS-trusted root (exported from the System keychain) only for the scratchpad playwright install command; no certificate validation was disabled and no repo/global configuration was changed.

During repeated browser-evidence runs, the server's own auth rate limiter (RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX, default 10/15min) correctly returned 429 after enough automated login attempts; this positively confirms D-AUTH rate-limiting is effective. The server was restarted once with RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX=1000 for the remainder of the browser-evidence pass only, to give the automated walk headroom; the dedicated low-limit rate-limit integration test was re-run unmodified afterward and still passes.

One console message class appeared on every Login-page load in the browser evidence pass: a browser-generated 'Failed to load resource: ... 401' network log line, from AuthProvider's intentional, unauthenticated GET /auth/me bootstrap check (needed so PublicOnlyRoute can redirect an already-authenticated visitor away from Login). This is not a JS exception (zero pageerror events were recorded) and is not explicit app-level console.error usage (confirmed by grep: no console.* calls in api/client.js, api/hooks.js, or AuthProvider.jsx). Treated as a resolved/understood artifact rather than an 'unresolved' console error per the roadmap's D-RESP-F7 wording, and disclosed here rather than omitted.

resolvedIssues.title: Real horizontal-scroll capability on the Insights page at the 320px supported viewport
resolvedIssues.expected: No horizontal scroll or clipped controls at any supported viewport (320-1440px), per D-RESP-F1 and the roadmap's mobile-320-to-desktop-1440 responsive requirement.
resolvedIssues.actual: At a 320px viewport, document.documentElement.scrollWidth (371px) exceeds clientWidth (320px) on the Insights page only (Budget and Login confirmed clean at 320px this session). Root cause: the shared .visually-hidden utility class (client/src/styles/global.css lines 62-72, used by client/src/features/insights/charts/VisuallyHiddenTable.jsx for all three charts' accessible data tables) sets width:1px, but Chromium's automatic table-layout algorithm ignores that explicit width for <table> elements and sizes them to their min-content width instead (measured 269-335px for the three hidden tables). The widest one (the 7-column cumulative cash-flow table) pushes the page 51px past a 320px viewport. The defect is invisible in a static screenshot (the content stays visually clipped via clip-path: inset(50%)) but is a real, reproducible layout overflow found via DOM measurement.
resolvedIssues.reproduction: Load /insights at a 320px-wide viewport while authenticated; evaluate document.documentElement.scrollWidth > document.documentElement.clientWidth in the browser console (returns true). See insights-320-overflow-diagnostic.json for per-table computed widths.
resolvedIssues.suggestedFix: Add table-layout: fixed (and/or an explicit small max-width plus white-space handling) to the .visually-hidden rule, or apply a table-specific hidden-table variant class, so <table> elements collapse to 1px like other elements. Not fixed in this test-only phase per the developer-loop skill (Test phase must not modify product code); recommend as the first task of the next fix cycle.
resolvedIssues.resolution: Fixed in fix cycle 01 (2026-07-31). The visually-hidden class was moved from the <table> to a 1px overflow-hidden <div> wrapper in VisuallyHiddenTable.jsx (a block wrapper honors width:1px and clips the table out of the layout), with a table-layout:fixed defense rule and documentation added to global.css and a structural regression test added to client/tests/InsightsPage.test.jsx. Chromium re-measurement: scrollWidth exactly 320 on Login, Budget, and Insights at a 320px viewport; every hidden wrapper measures 1px.

resolvedIssues.title: npm run format:check fails across the repository, including 32 real product source files
resolvedIssues.expected: Per this self-test assignment and the developer-loop skill's Test step 1 ('Run formatting/lint...'), npm run format:check should exit 0.
resolvedIssues.actual: npm run format:check exits 1, flagging 90 files. No .prettierignore exists in the repo, so the run also flags non-product files that should arguably never be prettier-formatted (docs/design/figma-kit/** design-kit source files that must stay byte-identical to the design tool's export, .workflow evidence markdown, tools/**). Separately from that noise, 32 real product source files under server/src/** and client/src/** genuinely violate the repo's own .prettierrc.json (printWidth 90) with plain line-wrapping differences (e.g. server/src/services/calc.js has three lines that exceed 90 columns and would be re-wrapped by `prettier --write`). npm run lint (eslint) was run at every stage per build-report.md, but npm run format:check does not appear to have been run in any prior batch.
resolvedIssues.reproduction: npm run format:check from the repo root; npx prettier --check server/src client/src isolates the 32 real product-file violations from the vendor/docs noise.
resolvedIssues.suggestedFix: Add a .prettierignore excluding docs/design/figma-kit/**, .workflow/**, and generated/vendor files; run `prettier --write` on the 32 real product-source files. Not fixed in this test-only phase per the developer-loop skill (Test phase must not modify product code); recommend as a task of the next fix cycle.
resolvedIssues.resolution: Fixed in fix cycle 01 (2026-07-31). Added a justified .prettierignore (workflow reports, tools/, read-only design/product/workflow sources, CLAUDE.md, and tokens.css for the D-FND-D1 byte-identity invariant), then ran npx prettier --write . over the remaining files: 66 files reformatted including all 32 flagged product source files. npm run format:check now exits 0. Zero behavior change proven by full green lint/unit/component/integration/coverage/build/smoke runs after the rewrite (and green unit/component runs immediately before).
